title: Peripheral T-cell lymphoma
subtitle: Nodal PTCL · ALCL · NK/T · ATLL · rare extranodal subtypes — CD30 and ALK status pick the induction; ALK+ ALCL is the only subtype CHOP-like therapy reliably cures
source: Compiled from the Stanford Oncology Handbook 2025, Lymphoma: Non-Hodgkin, T-cell lymphoma · NCCN · primary trial reports and FDA actions verified against PubMed, September 2026.

blocks.heading: Entities — WHO-HAEM5 / ICC 2022
rows: Diagnosis of exclusion; CD4 > CD8, loss of CD5/CD7 common. GATA3-high subset does worse than TBX21

Formerly AITL (ICC: follicular helper T-cell lymphoma). Older adults; rash, effusions, polyclonal hypergammaglobulinemia, Coombs+ hemolysis, EBV+ B-blasts. PD-1, CXCL13, ICOS, BCL6, CD10. TET2, DNMT3A, IDH2 R172, RHOA G17V. Follicular and NOS types share the TFH phenotype
Younger; NPM1::ALK t(2;5); strong uniform CD30. 5-yr OS ~85% — the good one
Textured implants; late seroma or capsular mass, CD30+ ALK−. Tap the seroma → cytology + CD30
WHO-HAEM5 drops “nasal type.” EBV+ always, CD56+, cCD3ε+, surface CD3−; angiocentric, necrotic mid-face mass; Asia and Latin America
HTLV-1; Japan, Caribbean. CD4+CD25+ “flower cells,” hypercalcemia, lytic lesions, skin
EATL: celiac (refractory sprue). MEITL (old “type II EATL”): no celiac, CD8+CD56+, SETD2 loss. Perforation risk
γδ TCR; young men, IBD on anti-TNF + thiopurine; hepatosplenomegaly, sinusoidal marrow, no nodes. Dismal
blocks.footnote: Frequencies from the International T-cell Project (Vose, JCO 2008, n=1,153) — 10% of referral diagnoses were misclassified, so insist on expert hematopathology review.

boxes: salvage (ICE, GDP, DHAP) or single agent →
Match the agent to the biology
concurrent DeVIC or sequential P-GemOx / DDGP
follow plasma EBV DNA as the tumor marker

blocks.heading: Workup
items: Excisional or core biopsy with T-cell panel, CD30 (% of cells), ALK, TFH markers, EBER; TCR clonality. ALK− ALCL → DUSP22 and TP63 FISH
PET/CT, marrow biopsy, LDH, HTLV-1 serology (and calcium) in anyone at risk; plasma EBV DNA in NK/T and AITL
HBV/HCV/HIV; echo before anthracycline. Nasal NK/T: MRI of the nasopharynx + ENT exam
ATLL: screen for Strongyloides (co-endemic with HTLV-1) before steroids

blocks.heading: Prognosis — PIT and IPI
blocks.footnote: PIT (Gallamini, Blood 2004): age >60, LDH >ULN, ECOG ≥2, marrow involvement. The IPI also stratifies PTCL and is the stratifier in ECHELON-2. NK/T uses PINK (age >60, stage III–IV, distant nodes, non-nasal primary; 3-yr OS 81/62/25% for 0/1/≥2); PINK-E adds detectable EBV DNA.

blocks.heading: ATLL and rare subtypes
items: ATLL subtypes (Shimoyama): acute, lymphoma, chronic (unfavorable if LDH, BUN or albumin abnormal), smoldering. AZT + IFN-α (meta-analysis, n=254): 5-yr OS 46% with first-line antivirals — benefit in acute, chronic and smoldering, while lymphoma type does better with chemo

mLSG15 (VCAP-AMP-VECP) beat biweekly CHOP on CR (40% vs 25%), 3-yr OS 24% vs 13% (NS). Mogamulizumab: R/R ATLL ORR 50% (Japan-approved, not US). Given <50 d before allo-HCT it raises severe GVHD and NRM (1-yr OS 32% vs 49%)
BIA-ALCL: disease confined to capsule/seroma → total en bloc capsulectomy + implant removal (both sides) is usually curative; nodal or unresectable → BV-CHP
Hepatosplenic: CHOP fails — ICE or IVAC-type induction, then allo-HCT in CR1
EATL/MEITL: nutrition + surgical review for perforation; IVE/MTX (Newcastle) → auto-HCT. AITL: steroids/cyclosporine for immune flares; watch for concurrent EBV+ B-cell lymphoma

pages.subtitle: Page 2 — frontline evidence, relapsed disease, NK/T-cell lymphoma and toxicity

blocks.heading: Frontline evidence
items: ECHELON-2 (BV-CHP vs CHOP, CD30 ≥10%): PFS HR 0.71, OS HR 0.66 — the only regimen to beat CHOP on survival. 5-yr PFS 51% vs 43%, OS 70% vs 61%

But the benefit sits in systemic ALCL (70% of enrollment; 5-yr PFS HR 0.55). PTCL-NOS HR 0.75 (NS); AITL favored CHOP (small n). The label is sALCL or other CD30-expressing PTCL; outside ALCL it is a reasonable, not proven, choice
CD30 threshold was ≥10% by local IHC; retreatment with BV at relapse after BV-CHP still gave ORR 59%
CHOEP (DSHNHL pooled analysis): etoposide improved 3-yr EFS 75% vs 51% in age ≤60 with normal LDH; over 60, CHOP-21 stays standard

Auto-HCT in CR1 — never randomized. NLG-T-01 (CHOEP-14 → ASCT, ALK+ excluded): 5-yr OS 51%, PFS 44%, TRM 4%. COMPLETE cohort: ASCT in CR1 OS HR 0.37, driven by AITL; a LYSA registry analysis found no benefit. Offer it to fit non-ALK+ patients in CR, especially AITL and higher IPI

blocks.heading: Extranodal NK/T-cell lymphoma
items: Anthracyclines fail — tumor cells express P-glycoprotein (MDR1). Build regimens on L-asparaginase/pegaspargase, methotrexate, gemcitabine, platinum, etoposide
Localized: radiation is the backbone. DeVIC ×3 + concurrent RT 50 Gy (JCOG0211): 2-yr OS 78% vs 45% historical RT alone. Sequential/sandwich P-GemOx or DDGP + RT is the common alternative
Advanced: DDGP beat SMILE in a randomized trial (n=87; PFS HR 0.42, OS HR 0.41, 5-yr OS 74% vs 52%, less myelosuppression). SMILE: ORR 79% but grade 4 neutropenia 92% — require ALC ≥500
EBV DNA in plasma: detectable at diagnosis is adverse (PINK-E); persistent after therapy predicts relapse
R/R after asparaginase: PD-1 blockade — pembrolizumab responded in 7/7 (Kwong, Blood 2017); off-label in the US. Consolidate responders with allo-HCT

blocks.heading: Relapsed / refractory agents — and their US status
rows: R/R sALCL ORR 86%, CR 57% (Pro, JCO 2012). Regular approval. Activity in CD30+ non-ALCL is lower and not CD30-level dependent
PROPEL: ORR 29%, DOR 10.1 mo, PFS 3.5 mo. Accelerated approval 2009 — still unconfirmed; the confirmatory trial will not read out before ~2030
BELIEF: ORR 26%, CR 11%, DOR 13.6 mo, but PFS 1.6 mo. Accelerated 2014, unconfirmed — ODAC (Nov 2023) criticized both delays. Least myelosuppressive; OK with low platelets
ORR 25%, DOR 17 mo. PTCL indication withdrawn 2021 (Ro-CHOP negative) — still NCCN-listed and still FDA-approved for CTCL
PRIMO (JCO 2026, n=123): ORR 48%, CR 33%, but PFS 3.4 mo; AITL ORR 62%, CR 51%, PFS 8.3 mo. Not FDA-approved for PTCL (phase 3 TERZO ongoing)
VALENTINE-PTCL01: ORR 44% (52/119). Approved in Japan (ATLL 2022, PTCL June 2024); not US-approved
JACKPOT8 B: ORR 44%, CR 24% (94% Asian). Conditional approval in China (June 2024); US fast-track only
Crizotinib FDA-approved Jan 2021 for age 1–21 (ORR 88%); adults off-label. Alectinib, brigatinib, lorlatinib also active
Gemcitabine, bendamustine (ORR 50%, PFS 3.6 mo), lenalidomide (AITL), azacitidine in TET2-mutant TFH, cyclosporine for AITL immune phenomena
blocks.footnote: Response rates are all single-arm and PFS is short — use these to bridge a responder to allo-HCT, the only strategy with a durable plateau in R/R PTCL.

blocks.heading: Toxicity and monitoring
items: Brentuximab: peripheral neuropathy — hold for grade 3, dose-reduce for grade 2. PML (boxed warning); pancreatitis. Never with bleomycin (pulmonary toxicity)
Pralatrexate: mucositis is dose-limiting and prevented by B12/folate; check CBC weekly; reduce for CrCl <30
HDAC inhibitors: thrombocytopenia, nausea, fatigue, QTc — ECG, keep K and Mg replete. Belinostat: UGT1A1 genotype guides the dose
Duvelisib boxed warnings: fatal infections, colitis/diarrhea, severe skin reactions, pneumonitis; transaminitis. Mandatory PJP prophylaxis; CMV monitoring
Asparaginase: hypersensitivity, pancreatitis, hepatotoxicity, hypofibrinogenemia and thrombosis, hyperglycemia. Check fibrinogen, lipase, LFTs, glucose each cycle
HD-MTX (SMILE): hydration + urine alkalinization (pH ≥7), MTX levels, leucovorin rescue; glucarpidase if delayed clearance with AKI; stop PPIs, TMP-SMX, NSAIDs around the dose
Ifosfamide: mesna; watch for encephalopathy (methylene blue) and Fanconi-type nephrotoxicity
ALK inhibitors: crizotinib — visual disturbance, transaminitis, QTc, bradycardia
Prophylaxis: acyclovir + TMP-SMX with HDAC, duvelisib, SMILE, alemtuzumab; entecavir if HBcAb+

pages.subtitle: Page 3 — regimen dosing and key trials

blocks.heading: Regimen dosing
rows: Brentuximab 1.8 mg/kg (max 180 mg) + cyclophosphamide 750 mg/m² + doxorubicin 50 mg/m² d1, prednisone 100 mg d1–5 — q21d ×6–8. No vincristine. Primary G-CSF
CHOP as above + vincristine 1.4 mg/m² (max 2) d1; CHOEP adds etoposide 100 mg/m² d1–3 — q21d ×6 (NLG used CHOEP-14)
1.8 mg/kg IV q21d up to 16 cycles; 1.2 mg/kg if Child-Pugh A or neuropathy grade 2
30 mg/m² IV push weekly ×6 q7wk. Folic acid 1–1.25 mg daily from 7–10 d before until 30 d after; B12 1 mg IM q8–10 wk. Leucovorin mouthwash for mucositis
1,000 mg/m² IV over 30 min d1–5 q21d; 750 mg/m² if UGT1A1*28 homozygous
14 mg/m² IV over 4 h d1, 8, 15 q28d — K ≥4, Mg ≥2 before each dose; QTc
75 mg PO BID ×2 cycles, then 25 mg BID, q28d continuous. PJP + HSV/VZV prophylaxis
Dexamethasone 40 mg d1–3 + ifosfamide 1,000 mg/m² d1–3 (+ mesna) + etoposide 67 mg/m² d1–3 + carboplatin 200 mg/m² d1 — q21d ×3, concurrent RT 50 Gy
Dexamethasone 15 mg/m² d1–5 + cisplatin 20 mg/m² d1–4 + gemcitabine 800 mg/m² d1, 8 + pegaspargase 2,500 IU/m² d1 — q21d ×6

MTX 2 g/m² d1 (leucovorin from 24 h) · ifosfamide 1.5 g/m² + mesna, dexamethasone 40 mg, etoposide 100 mg/m² d2–4 · pegaspargase 2,000 U/m² d7 once MTX <0.04 µM — q28d ×2–6. Urine alkalinization for HD-MTX
High-dose oral zidovudine + daily SC interferon-α, continued indefinitely while responding — no randomized dosing standard; follow the treating center's protocol
blocks.footnote: DDGP doses are from the Chinese trial protocol (Li, Clin Cancer Res 2016). Interferon alfa-2b (Intron A) is off the US market — pegylated IFN is the practical substitute.

blocks.heading: Key trials
rows: BV-CHP vs CHOP: mPFS 48.2 vs 20.8 mo, HR 0.71; OS HR 0.66; 5-yr OS 70% vs 61%. Benefit concentrated in sALCL
CHOEP-14 → ASCT: 72% reached transplant; 5-yr PFS 44%, OS 51%, TRM 4%
Pralatrexate: ORR 29%, DOR 10.1 mo, PFS 3.5 mo — accelerated approval, unconfirmed
Belinostat: ORR 26%, CR 11%, DOR 13.6 mo, PFS 1.6 mo
Duvelisib: ORR 48%, CR 33%; AITL ORR 62%, CR 51%. Not FDA-approved for PTCL
Valemetostat: ORR 44%. Approved in Japan only
DeVIC + RT 50 Gy: 2-yr OS 78% vs 45% historical RT alone
PFS HR 0.42, OS HR 0.41; 5-yr OS 74% vs 52%; less myelosuppression
mLSG15 vs CHOP-14: CR 40% vs 25%; 3-yr OS 24% vs 13% (NS)
First-line antivirals: 5-yr OS 46%; benefit in leukemic subtypes, not lymphoma type
